ownership.quote: On June 28, 2016, they incorporated Vast.ai. ... Jake Cannell and Christian Horne incorporate Vast.ai as a Delaware C Corporation.

stage.quote: Vast.ai launches — not with a press release, but the way honest products launch: to friends, family, and a post on Reddit. ... 2025 40+ employees, two offices, SOC 2 certified ... The infrastructure that makes AI open is now an institution.
stage.note: Vast.ai's own About/press pages narrate a self-funded, founder-built growth story (2016 incorporation to 40+ employees / two offices by 2025) with no mention of any investor or funding round anywhere on the site, and the company runs a generic 'Investor Inquiries' contact form rather than announcing any raise. A Google AI-generated search summary asserted an unsourced ~$4M seed round in July 2024, but no primary source, press article, or aggregator page (Crunchbase/PitchBook were inaccessible; no TechCrunch/press coverage found) could be located to confirm this, so it is not treated as confirmed. Do not confuse with 'VAST Data' (enterprise storage, ~$1.4B raised, $30B valuation) or 'Vast Space' (aerospace) or the Chinese 3D-AI startup 'Tripo/Vast' — all unrelated companies with similar names.

note: GPU rental/cloud marketplace (peer-to-peer + data-center 'Secure Cloud'), founded 2016 by Jake Cannell (CEO) and Christian Horne, launched publicly Sept 2018; Travis Cannell (COO) joined 2022. HQ Los Angeles (since 2024) plus a San Francisco engineering office (2025); SOC 2 Type I certified (2025). No accelerator affiliation, funding round, or named investor could be confirmed from primary sources within the research window; company presents itself as an organically grown, founder-built company. Search-engine access in this environment was heavily rate-limited/blocked (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Crunchbase, PitchBook, Tracxn largely inaccessible), which constrained verification — treat funding/revenue fields as an incomplete picture rather than proof of 'no funding ever raised'.
